item.title: PFT's Week 3 2026 NFL power rankings
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Seahawks continue to rule the roost.
item.content:encoded:
1. Seahawks (last week No. 1; 2-0): No Darnold? No problem.

2. Bills (No. 2; 2-0): September wins are celebratory. January wins are mandatory.

3. Bengals (No. 7; 2-0): Joe Burrow can't keep taking these kinds of beatings.

4. Chiefs (No. 8; 2-0): Kenneth Walker III could become one of the best free-agent signings ever.

5. 49ers (No. 10; 2-0): Brock Purdy is making a push for the list of top-10 quarterbacks. Maybe the top five.

6. Broncos (No. 12; 1-1): Jaylen Waddle arrives, a few days later than they'd hoped.

7. Jaguars (No. 5; 1-1): They should just make Travis Hunter a full-time CB and be done with it.

8. Eagles (No. 9; 2-0): In any game, the only stat that matters is points scored vs. points allowed.

9. Rams (No. 11; 1-1): Fortunately, they didn't fly back from Australia the day before the Week 2 game.

10. Texans (No. 4; 0-2): The offense is letting down the defense.

11. Vikings (No. 15; 2-0): The defense has a flair for showing up in the biggest possible moments.

12. Bears (No. 3; 1-1): Don't sleep on West Virginia native Tyson Bagent.

13. Ravens (No. 6; 1-1): The Ravens seem to have a random head-scratcher at home every year. They'll need to make the loss to the Saints an aberration.

14. Patriots (No. 13; 1-1): At this rate, they won't have to worry about a difficult negotiation with Drake Maye in 2027.

15. Saints (No. 21; 1-1): The Saints are the best team no one is paying attention to.

16. Lions (No. 14; 1-1): The fans got spoiled by 2023 and 2024.

17. Giants (No. 16; 1-1): At some point, they probably should have double-covered Davante Adams.

18. Steelers (No. 17; 1-1): Remember when the unofficial media talking point was Mike McCarthy's high level of attention to detail?

19. Packers (No. 20; 1-1): Sometimes, a win feels like a loss.

20. Cowboys (No. 22; 1-1): The defense is still a work in progress.

21. Panthers (No. 23; 1-1): Bryce Young is finally becoming exactly what the Panthers hoped he'd be.

22. Raiders (No. 27; 2-0): Fernando Mendoza may be sitting for a while.

23. Browns (No. 32; 1-1): Sunday's home opener could get very interesting.

24. Cardinals (No. 18; 1-1): They may find out the hard way that the Chargers are just really bad.

25. Chargers (No. 19; 0-2): At least they do really good schedule-release videos.

26. Buccaneers (No. 24; 0-2): Where have you gone, Mike Evans?

27. Colts (No. 25; 0-2): The Colts got a gift in overtime, and they refused to take it.

28. Jets (No. 26; 1-1): Aaron Glenn continues to do himself no favors.

29. Titans (No. 30; 0-2): "We're tied for second place in the division!"

30. Commanders (No. 28; 0-2): Dan Quinn's time may be running out.

31. Dolphins (No. 31; 0-2): Arch Manning will look good in aqua.

32. Falcons (No. 29; 0-2): The country's not ready for three straight prime-time Falcons games.

item.title: Kyle Shanahan: Mike Evans' hip injury will have to be managed this week
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The 49ers have a few injury concerns entering Week 3, including one to veteran receiver Mike Evans.
item.content:encoded:
The 49ers have a few injury concerns entering Week 3, including one to veteran receiver Mike Evans.

Via Nick Wagoner of ESPN, head coach Kyle Shanahan said on Monday that Evans will “have to be managed this week” as the wideout deals with a hip injury.

Evans exited Sunday’s 35-13 victory over the Dolphins in the second half and did not return. Shanahan noted postgame that the injury didn’t appear to be serious, and if the game had been closer, Evans could have returned.

Defensive lineman Romello Height has a broken hand and will need surgery. There’s an outside chance he could be available in Week 3.

Receiver Demarcus Robinson and defensive tackle James Thompson Jr. both have suffered high-ankle sprains. Robinson is a candidate for injured reserve, with the idea he could return.

But Shanahan also noted that the 49ers will have to be selective about who does and who doesn’t go to IR, because the team is running out of slots for players who can return from the list.

Additionally, defensive lineman Mykel Williams will not start practicing this week as he is still on the physically unable to perform list. He is more likely to be back for practice entering Week 4.

item.title: Aaron Glenn: No regrets about how we handled end of regulation against Packers
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn's late-game decision-making came under fire in Sunday's overtime loss to the Packers, but he doesn't feel any differently about his choices after a night to sleep on it.
item.content:encoded:
Jets head coach Aaron Glenn's late-game decision-making came under fire in Sunday's overtime loss to the Packers, but he doesn't feel any differently about his choices after a night to sleep on it.

After the 20-17 loss, Glenn said he never considered calling a timeout when the Packers faced a fourth down near midfield with about a minute left in regulation. The Packers wound up running the clock down and taking a delay of game penalty before trying a Hail Mary on the final snap of the game.

On Sunday, Glenn said he didn't want the team's offense to be backed up after a punt and reiterated that on a Monday video conference while expressing no doubt about the course of action he chose for the team.

"Between me and our game management guys, our analytical guys, we talk through those situations quite a bit," Glenn said. "That situation actually came up in a number of our conversations. When we have the punter at the logo, we don't want to put ourselves in a situation where we get our guys in a backed up situation. I know we talk about getting our offense going in that situation, but the thing is they had two timeouts also. If you put yourself in a backed up situation and things don't go as planned, I think you’re giving the other team an opportunity to go out there and make a play. I just felt like that was the right decision to do at that point and we actually wanted to play for overtime when it came to that.”

Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said on Sunday that he was "really confused" by how Glenn handled the situation, which could be translated to being really thankful that Glenn allowed the Packers to control how the final minute of regulation played out.

item.title: Jayden Daniels consulting specialists after dislocating left elbow Sunday
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels dislocated his left elbow during Sunday's loss to the Cowboys and is now trying to sort out how long he will be out of action as a result of the injury.
item.content:encoded:
Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels dislocated his left elbow during Sunday's loss to the Cowboys and is now trying to sort out how long he will be out of action as a result of the injury.

Daniels went for imaging on the elbow on Monday and head coach Dan Quinn said at a Monday press conference that he will now solicit opinions from specialists about the next courses of action.

Daniels suffered the same injury during the 2025 season and missed four games before returning to the lineup. He aggravated the injury in his return and then missed the final four games of the season. It's not clear if the past injuries will play a role in how Daniels and doctors choose to treat Sunday's dislocation.

Quinn said on Sunday that his team will "rally around" backup quarterback Marcus Mariota and confirmed on Monday that Mariota will start against the Seahawks in a Week 3 home game.

item.title: Kyler Murray clears concussion protocol, set to start Week 3 vs. Bucs
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Murray will be back in the starting lineup for next week's game after Carson Wentz started Week 2.
item.content:encoded:
Kyler Murray is set to return to the starting lineup.

Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell told reporters in his Monday press conference that Murray has cleared concussion protocol and is on schedule to play in the team’s matchup with the Buccaneers.

“Kyler has cleared the final phase of the protocol,” O’Connell said. “He’s doing great, he’ll be cleared, and he will start this week against Tampa Bay.”

Murray went down early in the Week 1 win over the Packers when he was hit while trying to slide on a scramble. He departed that contest having completed 3-of-5 passes for 18 yards with an interception.

Carson Wentz replaced Murray for the last two weeks. He was 11-of-20 for 143 yards in Sunday’s victory over the Bears. O’Connell praised how steady Wentz has been as a backup.

In five games last year for the Cardinals, Murray completed 68.3 percent of his throws for 962 yards with six touchdowns and three interceptions.

Also on the injury front, O’Connell said Ty Ingram-Dawkins (hip) is day-to-day and Brett Thorson has a hamstring issue.

item.title: Sean McVay attributes Week 1 loss to "dumbass coach that makes travel plans"
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: After the Rams beat the Giants on Monday night, McVay took the blame for the Week 1 debacle in Australia.
item.content:encoded:
The Rams looked like Super Bowl contenders on Monday night against the Giants, a significant improvement from their Week 1 loss to the 49ers in Australia. Rams coach Sean McVay blamed the Rams' much-discussed travel plans, and himself, for that Week 1 loss.

McVay was asked after the win over the Giants why the Rams looked so different than they did in Australia, and McVay said it was primarily about his own decision to arrive in Australia only a day before the game.

"Sometimes you win, sometimes you learn and sometimes you have a dumbass coach that makes travel plans that puts you in bad spots," McVay said.

The Rams' decision to arrive in Australia only about 24 hours before kickoff was an attempt not to acclimate to the time change at all. The 49ers arrived in Australia a week early and were well acclimated. The 49ers won 27-7, and the Rams' travel schedule has been heavily scrutinized.

McVay took the blame for not having his team ready to play in Australia, but they were very ready to play in Los Angeles on Monday night, winning 28-6.

item.title: Dan Campbell on Kerby Joseph: We're trying to get him back, but he's not ready
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Lions have struggled in the secondary through the first two weeks of the season and part of the reason why they're having a hard time is the absence of safeties Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph.
item.content:encoded:
The Lions have struggled in the secondary through the first two weeks of the season and part of the reason why they're having a hard time is the absence of safeties Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph.

Head coach Dan Campbell said at a Monday press conference that Branch, who is coming off a torn Achilles, is probably closer to returning from the physically unable to perform list than Joseph. Joseph has been dealing with knee problems since early last season and Campbell was asked on 97.1 The Ticket on Tuesday what he would say to someone who wonders if Joseph is going to play at all this season.

"I wish I could make you feel good," Campbell said. "I can’t make you feel good. It’s going to come as it comes, and he’s not ready. We’re trying to get him there as fast as we can, and we’re trying to be as smart about it as we can. If he’s ready, when he’s ready, of course we want to play him and get him on the field."

The Lions lost another safety when Avonte Maddox went down in Week 2 and they added veteran Jalen Mills to their practice squad on Monday to help bolster their depth. Barring a major change for Joseph, they may remain on the search for help at the back end of the defense all year.

item.title: Giants receiver Malik Nabers suffers apparent arm injury
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Nabers exits in considerable pain.
item.content:encoded:
It's been a bad night for the New York Giants.

After losing quarterback Jaxson Dart to a knee injury (he's questionable to return), receiver Malik Nabers has been injured.

Nabers left the game after apparently injuring his upper right arm.

He tried to make a contested catch while being covered by Rams cornerback Trent McDuffie. Immediately after the play, Nabers put his left hand over the area between his bicep and shoulder.

Nabers was in considerable pain. His status will be updated, presumably sooner than later.

The Giants trail the Rams, 7-0.

Nabers returned to action in Week 1 after suffering a torn ACL in his knee last September. It was uncertain whether he'd play in the opener until pregame warmups. He caught six passes for 69 yards against the Cowboys. He has one catch for one yard against the Rams.

UPDATE 9:02 p.m. ET: It's being described as a shoulder injury for Nabers.

item.title: Monday Night Football: Rams roll Giants 28-6 after Jaxson Dart's departure
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Matthew Stafford threw four touchdown passes, two to Davante Adams, who had 195 yards.
item.content:encoded:
The Rams are back . . . and so is Aaron Donald.

Eleven days after a lackluster performance against the 49ers in Australia, the Rams rebounded with a dominant 28-6 victory over the Giants in Donald's season debut. Both teams are 1-1.

The Rams might have won big anyway, but the Giants had no chance after Jaxson Dart injured his left knee on the first drive. The Giants had only 182 yards, and Jameis Winston was 11-of-27 for 111 yards and an interception.

The Giants crossed midfield six times, but punted six times, kicked two field goals, threw an interception and once turned it over on downs in their 10 possessions. It was as depressing as their season-opening win over the Cowboys was encouraging.

Donald, playing his first game in 981 days after unretiring Aug. 30, made three tackles, including a tackle for loss.

The Rams gained 481 yards despite playing without wide receiver Puka Nacua. Davante Adams more than made up for Nacua's absence, catching eight passes for 195 yards and two touchdowns.

Matthew Stafford threw touchdown passes of 31 and 11 yards to Adams, 10 yards to running back Kyren Williams and 5 yards to tight end Terrance Ferguson. Stafford was 22-of-31 for 327 yards with an interception to go with the four touchdowns.

Williams ran for 85 yards on 12 carries, but he did lose a fumble. Blake Corum had 12 carries for 79 yards.

Giants safety Jevon Holland totaled eight tackles, an interception, two forced fumbles and a fumble recovery in an elite performance.

item.title: Michael Penix Jr. will start for Falcons on Thursday night
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: 2024 first-rounder will return from November 2025 ACL tear.
item.content:encoded:
The Falcons' quarterback carousel has finally landed on their first-round draft pick from 2024.

The team has announced that Michael Penix Jr. will start in Thursday night's game against the Packers at Lambeau Field.

Penix suffered a torn ACL in November 2025. He fully participated in practice before both regular-season games, but he was not ready to play.

Some would say that, if he's going to be ready to play on Thursday, he could have played on Sunday against the Panthers.

Instead, it was Cooper Rush. Rush was removed in the third quarter for undrafted rookie Jack Strand. In combination, they threw three interceptions and generated a passer rating of 28.8.

And so it will be Penix time for the 0-2 Falcons, whose next three games are scheduled to be played in prime time.

item.title: Monday Night Football: Puka Nacua is officially inactive with hip injury
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Aaron Donald may be back, but the Rams will not have one of their best offensive players for Monday night's matchup against the Giants.
item.content:encoded:
Aaron Donald may be back, but the Rams will not have one of their best offensive players for Monday night's matchup against the Giants.

Puka Nacua is officially inactive due to his hip injury.

Reports had indicated this was the way things were trending for Nacua, who did not practice on Friday or Saturday.

Nacua caught five passes for 74 yards in the Rams’ season-opening loss to the 49ers.

For the Giants, cornerback Deonte Banks and linebacker Micah McFadden are both inactive after they were listed as questionable.

New York’s remaining inactives are tight end Thomas Fidone, offensive lineman J.C. Davis, defensive lineman Bobby Jamison-Travis, defensive lineman Darius Alexander, and safety Jason Pinnock.

For the Rams, Nacua, receiver Jordan Whittington, safety Kamren Kinchens, receiver C.J. Daniels, guard Bill Murray, and quarterback Ty Simpson are inactive. Simpson is Los Angeles’ emergency third QB.

item.title: Brian Burns says his low ankle sprain is "nothing serious"
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Burns limped off the field and to the locker room on Monday night but said after the game he would be OK.
item.content:encoded:
Giants pass rusher Brian Burns limped off the field in obvious pain on Monday night, but in the locker room after the game, Burns said the medical diagnosis showed that the damage to his ankle wasn't as bad as it felt.

Burns said as he sat at his locker that he could feel his ankle getting stiff but the Giants' medical staff had told him it's a low ankle sprain that shouldn't cause him to miss much time.

“It eases my mind to know it’s not nothing serious," Burns said.

Burns said he's had similar injuries and knows how to rehab them so he can get back on the field quickly.

“I’ve dealt with this before,” Burns said. “It all depends on how fast you can get the swelling and inflammation down. I’m going to do everything possible to get as tamed as I can."

Burns said he would begin his rehab while on the flight from Los Angeles back to New York.

"The recovery process starts now, so it will be ice and compression until we get back to the facility and do more work on it, try to stay off it, keep it elevated," Burns said. "That's all you can do with sprains. I've dealt with it before."

Burns is one of the Giants' best defensive players, and on a night when quarterback Jaxson Dart, wide receiver Malik Nabers and left tackle Andrew Thomas all got hurt, a serious injury to Burns was the last thing the Giants needed. Fortunately, he's going to be OK.

item.title: Jaxson Dart is believed to have a sprained MCL
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: MRI is coming on Monday.
item.content:encoded:
The Giants have gotten some good news, for now, regarding quarterback Jaxson Dart's knee injury.

Via NFL Network, it's believed that Dart suffered a sprained MCL.

The assessment is based on a preliminary exam. X-rays were negative, and an MRI will be conducted on Tuesday.

After the game, coach John Harbaugh was asked about the report. "We'll know more tomorrow," Harbaugh said. "That's in the neighborhood of it, I would say. We'll get an MRI tomorrow and have a really good feel for it, and give you more information then."

The MCL can heal with rest and rehab, unless the tendon is completely torn.

If Dart misses time, Jameis Winston will continue to play in his place. On Monday night, Winston completed 11 of 27 passes for 111 yards and an interception.

The Giants host the Titans on Sunday, with the Cardinals next and a visit to the Commanders. So they could find a way to win some games, even if Dart is absent.

item.title: Ben Johnson: Caleb Williams week-to-week, likely will miss time
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: While Williams appears to have avoided a major hamstring injury, he is likely to be sidelined.
item.content:encoded:
Bears quarterback Caleb Williams avoided a major injury, but his hamstring is likely going to need some time to heal.

In a radio interview with ESPN 1000 Chicago on Monday, head coach Ben Johnson noted that Williams is likely to be sidelined for a bit.

"It sounds like it's going to be a week-to-week deal for him," Johnson said, via Courtney Cronin of ESPN. "I've got to still talk with our trainer. We'll do that here shortly and I'll have the lowdown from him. But it sounds like it's week-to-week, but will likely miss some time.”

Johnson added that the Bears “potentially” dodged a bullet with Williams’ injury not being more severe.

“You know, we’ll see,” Johnson said. “He’s tough and he comes back from these types of things, I think, better than the average human being. So, we’ll see.”

Williams was 15-of-26 for 138 yards with an interception before departing Sunday’s loss to the Vikings. He also rushed 42 yards on five carries.

Tyson Bagent is Chicago's backup quarterback.

The Bears will play the Eagles on Monday night in Week 3.

item.title: Aaron Donald: Game wasn't as fast as I thought
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Donald played his first game since 2023 on Monday night.
item.content:encoded:
SoFi Stadium got a jolt of energy before Monday night's game when Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald was the final defensive starter announced to the home crowd.

Donald said the response from that crowd "kind of amped me up a little bit" as he ran onto the field for the first time since deciding to end the retirement that started after the 2023 season. Donald did not travel to Australia for the opener and took more time to ramp himself up for his return to game action.

The result was three tackles and a tackle for loss while playing 33 of the team's 58 defensive snaps in Monday night's 28-6 win over the Giants. Donald said he would like to win "a little faster" when he's blocked one-on-one and that he feels like everything will feel more natural with a little more playing time under his belt.

"The game really wasn't as fast as I thought," Donald said, via the team's website. "It was more of me calming myself down, overrunning stuff or just my feet not being in the ground how they supposed to be, not trusting my eyes, little stuff like that. But playing the game, when I held out in '17, '18 it was the same way when I came back, it took a couple games to get going. It's a little different. I ain't played in two years, so I gotta watch the film, see what I did good, see what I did wrong, and just clean it up."

The plan was for the Rams to team Donald with Myles Garrett, but Garrett's knee injury leaves that on hold for the time being so all involved will hope that the weeks to come find Donald recovering even more of the game that made him a three-time defensive player of the year.

item.title: Matthew Stafford: We leaned on Davante Adams Monday and he came through for us
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Rams didn't have Puka Nacua for Monday night's game against the Giants, but the wide receiver's absence didn't wind up holding them back.
item.content:encoded:
The Rams didn't have Puka Nacua for Monday night's game against the Giants, but the wide receiver's absence didn't wind up holding them back.

Matthew Stafford found the groove that eluded the Rams in Week 1's loss to the 49ers and threw for 327 yards and four touchdowns in a 28-6 win. The first of those scores came late in the first quarter when he found a wide open Davante Adams for a 31-yard score and it would not be the last time Adams found holes in the Giants defense.

Adams used a double move to shake off Giants defenders for a 64-yard catch on the next Rams possession and he added his second touchdown catch of the night in the third quarter. The night ended with eight catches for 195 yards that Stafford said the Rams really needed given who wasn't available for the game.

"He's an elite player," Stafford said, via the team's website. "He made all sorts of plays today. [He] made contested catches. He ran great routes and got open. He did it all for us, and he's a guy that can do that. We understand that. We know it. And like I said, leaned on him big time tonight, and he came through for us."

The Rams will be hoping to have more hands on deck in Denver next weekend, but Monday was a reminder of how much they bring to the table even when they aren't playing with a full deck.

item.title: Dan Campbell: Lions don't know what we are yet
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Lions coach Dan Campbell says two games into the season is way too soon to know what kind of football team he has.
item.content:encoded:
Lions coach Dan Campbell says two games into the season is way too soon to know what kind of football team he has.

"We don't even know what we are yet, entirely. We don't know what we are," Campbell said. "The 2026 Detroit Lions' offense, defense, special teams, what do we really hang our hat on? We've got an idea on some of our go-to guys, our heavy hitters, but what do we really do well with those guys? And we won't, and I hate saying it, we're not gonna know until probably around the bye [Week 6]. Until we get a good four or five games, and you really start to figure out, this is what we can do and where we can really grow."

Campbell said the Lions' 41-31 loss to the Bills on Thursday night doesn't mean they're not a good team that will have a successful season.

"As bad as it was, it's not as bad as it appears to be," Campbell said. "And you clean a couple things up, you get guys right, you put guys in the right positions, one guy does what he's supposed to do, that leads to trust the other guy, now we can start cutting it loose and we get our confidence back, and the offense starts playing better, we start converting more, now all of a sudden you begin to get a little bit better, the floor begins to rise on where you're at. I'm not discouraged."

Now the Lions prepare for a home game against the Jets — where a loss would drop their record to 1-2 and raise even more questions about what kind of team the Lions are.

item.title: Todd Monken: Message to team after win is "So what, now what?"
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Browns got their first win of the season in Tampa on Sunday and it was also Todd Monken's first win as an NFL head coach.
item.content:encoded:
The Browns got their first win of the season in Tampa on Sunday and it was also Todd Monken's first win as an NFL head coach.

It has been almost four decades since Monken took his first college coaching job and the path to getting the victory included a lengthy weather delay before the Browns could shut the door on the Buccaneers for good. On Monday, Monken was asked if he ever thought that his first win would play out that way and his answer transitioned from saying it isn't about him to offering a reminder that the goal isn't just to win once.

"It’s a players’ game, and we got a lot to clean up, coaching and playing, and we took a giant step from Week 1 to Week 2," Monken said, via a transcript from the team. "So that’ll be the message we come back Wednesday is, ‘So what, now what?’ Are we willing to take that same jump? Or is it now, all of a sudden, we’ve arrived, because it’s week to week. You guys saw the scores, you guys know how this goes, every team’s a different matchup, and we didn’t turn the ball over, which helped us. In that first game we turned it over two of the first four drives, so basically, 'So what, now what?' What are we going to do this week to continue to improve? And we got the right guys to do it, that’s what I love about our group, because they’re going to be ready to go to work on Wednesday."

Sustained success has been elusive in Cleveland since the Browns re-entered the league in 1999 and Monken's response underscores how much the team still has to do in order to get where he wants them to be.

item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Word over the weekend was encouraging about quarterback Sam Darnold's recovery from the glute injury that kept him from playing in Week 2 and head coach Mike Macdonald brought more good news on Monday.
item.content:encoded:
Word over the weekend was encouraging about quarterback Sam Darnold's recovery from the glute injury that kept him from playing in Week 2 and head coach Mike Macdonald brought more good news on Monday.

Macdonald said that Darnold is expected to be on the field when the team returns to practice on Wednesday.

"Right now the plan is for him to be out there in some capacity, and we'll go from there," Macdonald said, via the team's website. "How much? We'll see from here to Wednesday what that number is, but right now that's the goal."

The answer to the question of how much work Darnold is able to do will be tied to his chances of being cleared to play against the Commanders in Week 3. Drew Lock handled things well in Sunday's rout of the Cardinals, so the 2-0 Seahawks will not have much reason to hurry Darnold back if the best course of action is a slower buildup to game action.

item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Monday night's game can't end soon enough for the Giants.
item.content:encoded:
Monday night's game can't end soon enough for the Giants.

Not only are they getting blown out by the Rams, but they have had injuries to some of their biggest players. Quarterback Jaxson Dart injured his left knee on the first possession and is standing on the sideline in street clothes.

Wide receiver Malik Nabers left briefly with a shoulder injury.

Now, pass rusher Brian Burns and left tackle Andrew Thomas are injured.

Thomas limped off late in the fourth quarter and Burns followed soon after.

Burns' injury looked serious as Rams center Coleman Shelton inadvertently rolled over Burns' left ankle, pinning it to the ground. He needed the assistance of two athletic trainers to get off the field.

The Giants did not have an update on Burns or Thomas before the game ended.

item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart left Monday night's game early with a knee injury, and he didn't return.
item.content:encoded:
Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart left Monday night's game early with a knee injury, and he didn't return.

It apparently wasn't his choice.

Via Jordan Raanan of ESPN, Dart wanted to return to the game. Obviously, the Giants wouldn't allow it.

Laura Rutledge of ESPN has added that the Giants eventually took Dart's uniform, preventing a return. She also said his limp is "very minor."

The specific diagnosis remains to be seen. Lip readers have spotted an interaction between coach John Harbaugh and a staffer during which Harbaugh possibly is being told Dart will be out 4-6 weeks.

That timeframe could point to an MCL injury. Obviously, however, no one knows for now. And the official diagnosis presumably is coming on Tuesday, after Dart gets an MRI.

item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Davante Adams is having a career day.
item.content:encoded:
Davante Adams is having a career day.

The Rams receiver has eight catches for 195 yards and two touchdowns. His second touchdown came on an 11-yard pass from Matthew Stafford and increased the Rams' lead to 21-3 over the Giants.

Adams' career-high for receiving yards is 206 on 11 catches while playing for the Packers against the Bengals in an overtime game in 2021.

It was Adams’ 119th career touchdown, ranking him seventh in NFL history. He is only two touchdown receptions behind Larry Fitzgerald, who is sixth on the list.

Stafford passed Philip Rivers for sixth on the all-time passing touchdowns list with his third of the night. He has 426 career passing touchdowns.

item.title: Jaxson Dart ruled out but "going to be OK"
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Giants quarterback hurt his left knee on the team's first possession of Monday Night Football.
item.content:encoded:
The Giants officially ruled out Jaxson Dart for the second half, but ESPN sideline reporter Laura Rutledge delivered a positive update from General Manager Joe Schoen.

The Giants are still evaluating the injury, with Dart getting an X-ray at SoFi Stadium, but Schoen told Rutledge that Dart is "going to be OK."

That presumably means Dart did not tear a ligament in his left knee and will return this season.

Coach John Harbaugh did not provide any information to Rutledge about Dart's injury in a halftime interview.

Dart was hurt on the Giants' first possession on a third-down play when Rams defenders Josaiah Stewart and Byron Young pressured him. Young hit Dart high, pushing him into Stewart, and, with Dart airborne, his left knee jammed into Stewart’s quad.

Dart remained on the turf with 11:20 left in the first quarter.

He went 3-for-5 for 20 yards before leaving.

Jameis Winston has replaced Dart and is 5-of-13 for 71 yards and an interception.

item.title: Monday Night Football: Matthew Stafford, Davante Adams have Rams up 14-3 at halftime
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Rams are playing without wide receiver Puka Nacua and pass rusher Myles Garrett.
item.content:encoded:
The Rams are playing without wide receiver Puka Nacua and pass rusher Myles Garrett. They haven't missed them so far tonight, with the Giants having lost quarterback Jaxson Dart on the first possession.

Stafford has thrown for 184 yards and two touchdowns, with Davante Adams catching five for 145 and a touchdown.

The Rams lead 14-3.

Rams defensive lineman Aaron Donald has three tackles, including one for loss, in his first game action in 981 days. Donald retired after the 2023 season but officially unretired Aug. 30.

Adams, 31, has not had a better game since Dec. 15, 2024, against the Jaguars when he caught nine passes for 198 yards and two touchdowns.

Stafford has completed 11 of 15 passes and has thrown a pick. His touchdowns covered 31 yards to Adams and 10 yards to running back Kyren Williams.

The Rams should have had three more points to end the half, but kicker Harrison Mevis missed a 43-yard try wide left on the final play of the half.

Giants safety Jevon Holland has done everything he can to keep his team in it. Holland, who had an interception of Dak Prescott last week, has an interception, a forced fumble and a recovered fumble.

At the end of a 5-yard Kyren Williams run late in the first half, Holland punched the ball out and recovered it at the Los Angeles 11. It was Williams' eighth career fumble.

The Giants had six possessions in the first half and four times crossed midfield with drives to the Los Angeles 43, 43, 18 and 3 without a touchdown. After Holland's fumble recovery, the Giants settled for Dominic Zvada's chip-shot, 24-yard field goal with 25 seconds left in the half.

Dart went 3-of-5 for 20 yards before injuring his left knee. Jameis Winston replaced him and was 4-of-12 for 58 yards and an interception, a throw straight to Rams cornerback Trent McDuffie in the end zone.

Cam Skattebo has only 18 yards on seven carries.

item.title: Long-time Bills radio voice John Murphy believes he lost credential over criticism of Joe Brady
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: In an age of sports media that features plenty of reporters and analysts who are on the payroll, directly or indirectly, of the teams and/or leagues they cover, some teams and leagues feel emboldened to take action against those who dare to cover them with scrutiny or criticism.
item.content:encoded:
In an age of sports media that features plenty of reporters and analysts who are on the payroll, directly or indirectly, of the teams and/or leagues they cover, some teams and leagues feel emboldened to take action against those who dare to cover them with scrutiny or criticism.

Long-time Bills radio voice John Murphy lost his press-box credential after writing a column regarding new coach Joe Brady for WIVB-TV, which is the official TV station of the team.

Via Alan Pergament of the Buffalo News, Murphy received a text from WIVB sports director Josh Reed two days after the column was posted that Murphy wouldn’t have a seat in the press box at the team's new stadium.

Said Murphy regarding whether he believed the denial was a result of his column, “I think so, but I don’t know.”

The denial was attributed to a policy against part-time workers getting credentials.

The Bills declined a request for comment from Pergament.

Murphy claims that Bills V.P. of marketing Chris Jenkins told Murphy he'd receive a credential for the season, and that Murphy was shown the seat he'd be using.

Murphy also said that his subsequent column predicting a 10-win season for the Bills wasn't posted by WIVB, after the station said it couldn't be published due to pressure from the Bills.

Murphy spent 34 years as an analyst and a radio voice for the Bills. He retired in 2023 after suffering a stroke.

“I feel pretty bad,” Murphy told Pergament. “[WIVB] didn’t fight for me. [The column] wasn’t that bad.”

It's not currently clear, and never may be known with certainty, whether the Bills retaliated against Murphy. Typically, such motivation isn't worn on the sleeve of the entity doing the retaliation.

If that's what's happening, it would be sad. And it possibly would be a manifestation of the extreme pressure the organization is feeling to justify the decision to fire coach Sean McDermott while promoting Brady and G.M. Brandon Beane.

item.description: Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford moved into a tie for sixth on the NFL's all-time passing touchdowns list on Monday night.
item.content:encoded:
Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford moved into a tie for sixth on the NFL's all-time passing touchdowns list on Monday night.

He tied Philip Rivers with his second touchdown of the night. Stafford's 10-yard scoring toss to running back Kyren Williams was the 425th of Stafford's career and gave the Rams a 14-0 lead with 11:07 left before halftime.

Brett Favre is fifth on the all-time list with 508, and Tom Brady is the leader with 649.

Stafford threw a 31-yard touchdown pass to Davante Adams in the first quarter. He nearly had a second touchdown to Adams, completing a 64-yard pass to Adams before safety Jevon Holland pulled down Adams at the Giants 14.

Adams has four catches for 118 yards and a touchdown.

Stafford is 10-of-12 for 157 yards and two touchdowns.

item.title: Darius Slayton agrees to terms with Colts
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: With receiver Alec Pierce expected to miss at least several weeks after aggravating his surgically repaired heel, the Colts need help at the position.
item.content:encoded:
With receiver Alec Pierce expected to miss at least several weeks after aggravating his surgically repaired heel, the Colts need help at the position.

They've gotten it, in the form of veteran receiver Darius Slayton. Via multiple reports, Slayton has agreed to terms with the Colts.

Earlier this month, the Giants cut Slayton. He was in the second year of a three-year, $36 million contract. The Giants owe him $9.75 million fully guaranteed in 2026. They'll get an offset for whatever he makes from the Colts.

Slayton spent seven years with the Giants. He has 296 career catches for 4,435 yards and 22 touchdowns.

The Colts have Pierce, Keenan Allen, Laquon Treadwell, Josh Downs, Ashton Dulin, and Deion Burks on the roster at the receiver position. Pierce likely will be put on injured reserve, which will create the roster spot for Slayton.
